Observed evidence: ANC participation shows a strong socioeconomic gradient across the pathway. Any ANC ranged from 53.9% in the poorest quintile to 95.0% in the richest. Among women reaching ANC4+, ANC8+ was 19.9% in the poorest versus 51.7% in the richest. The difference also remained among early initiators.
Model evidence: Household wealth was the leading full-cohort XGBoost SHAP predictor and remained the highest-ranked shared predictor after early ANC timing was added.
Programme-review cue: Review whether barriers affecting poorer women persist beyond initial ANC access and continue through repeated contacts.
Contextual lenses: Travel time; maternal occupation; pregnancy intention
Key caution: The analysis identifies an equity pattern but does not establish which financial, geographic or service mechanism causes it.

Observed evidence: ANC entry and subsequent attainment decline as travel time increases. Any ANC was 86.5% at 0–30 minutes versus 54.7% at >120 minutes. Among early initiators, ANC8+ was 48.2% at 0–30 minutes versus 18.5% at >120 minutes.
Model evidence: Travel time was among the strongest predictors in both the full-cohort and ANC-entry models and remained highly prominent after early ANC timing was introduced.
Programme-review cue: Review where geographic and repeated-travel burdens interfere with both ANC entry and sustained attendance.
Key caution: The empirical pattern does not determine which access or service-delivery response would be effective.

Observed evidence: The stage at which ANC gaps become visible differs across regions. Somali shows a major entry deficit, while Central Ethiopia, Tigray, South Ethiopia and Sidama show different patterns of weaker timing or later continuation. Afar shows a particularly strong travel-related entry difference.
Model evidence: Region was consistently among the leading predictors across algorithms and remained highly ranked after early ANC was added.
Programme-review cue: Diagnose the pathway stage responsible for each regional pattern before considering a programme response.
Contextual lenses: Travel time; religion; local service context
Key caution: Region is a contextual marker containing many social, geographic and health-system influences. It is not itself a causal mechanism.

Observed evidence: ANC8+ was 42.4% among early initiators compared with 11.1% among later initiators. However, 57.6% of early initiators still did not attain ANC8+, showing that timely initiation alone does not ensure completion of the recommended contact schedule.
Model evidence: Early ANC ranked first in permutation importance across all three extended models and first in XGBoost SHAP. Frozen model-response contrasts were positive across algorithms, but paired performance confidence intervals for adding early ANC included zero.
Programme-review cue: Review timely initiation and continuity after initiation as related but distinct programme problems.
Contextual lenses: Household wealth; travel time; region; maternal occupation
Key caution: Neither the observed difference nor the model-response contrast is a causal estimate of the effect of initiating ANC early.
